name: get_next_requirement
description:
Discover the next orchestration wave for the story the working copy's team
(its coding and QA agents) holds.

Discovery never selects another story. An explicit story must agree with that
assignment. Use `start_task` on offered requirements.

story_number.description: Optional story number; must match your active story

name: list_requirements
description:
List project requirements with their satisfaction status — filterable.

**The default is every requirement, satisfied and not, one row each, capped at
100** — `status` unset, `summary: false`, `limit: 100`. Those defaults are
deliberate and `parse_opts/1` says why: the tool predates its filters and
existing callers ask it for the full picture.

**For "where is the friction", ask for it:**

    summary: true, status: "unsatisfied"

Both parts matter. `summary: true` alone counts *all* requirements, which on
this project reads `implementation_file: 900` — a number that looks like a
catastrophic regression and is in fact 900 satisfied requirements. An agent
who takes it as friction goes hunting a break that does not exist; this
paragraph exists because that happened, off a moduledoc that claimed the
unfiltered default was a summary of unsatisfied requirements. It is neither.
With both set the same project reads 55.

The size warning is still real and is the reason `summary` exists: with a 500+
component project the raw per-entity dump runs 180k+ characters and can exceed
tool-response token limits. `limit` bounds it; the summary avoids it.

This is a read-only discovery tool — use it to understand the full picture
of what needs doing before picking a requirement to work on.

diagnostic.description: When `summary: true`, break out counts into `locally failing` vs `blocked by prereqs` (clamped). Useful for triage — distinguishes real friction from cascade effects. Default: false.

entity_id.description: Filter to one entity: a story's number or a component's id, as printed elsewhere. Combine with `entity_type` to disambiguate.

entity_type.description: Filter to one entity type — `project`, `story`, or `component`.

limit.description: Cap number of per-entity rows when `summary` is false. Default: 100. Bounds the response so a 500-component project doesn't return 180k+ chars.

module_filter.description: Substring match on the component module name (e.g., `Users.` to scope into a namespace).

requirement_name.description: Exact match on the requirement name (e.g., `bdd_specs_exist`, `ready_for_qa`, `implementation_file`).

status.description: Filter by satisfaction status — `satisfied` or `unsatisfied`. Default: no filter (returns both).

story_number.description: A story's number — the same as entity_type `story` with entity_id set to it

summary.description: Return aggregate counts by requirement name instead of per-entity rows. Default: `false` (per-entity view, matches the historical tool shape). Pass `true` for a friction breakdown that won't blow the token budget on big projects.

name: show_component_requirements
description: Show all requirements for a specific component, identified by module name or ID.

component.description: Component module name (e.g. 'MyApp.Accounts') or component ID

name: show_requirement
description:
Show a single requirement by name with full details including satisfaction
status, task module, and entity context.

entity_id.description: The entity to scope the lookup to: a story's number, or a component's id

story_number.description: A story's number — the same as entity_type `story` with entity_id set to it

name: show_story_requirements
description: Show all requirements for a specific story, identified by number or title.

story.description: Story title, when the number is not known

name: sync_project
description:
Sync project files and components.

Pulls remote issues into the local DB, scans the filesystem, classifies
and validates files, creates/updates components, and backfills file
ownership, then recomputes the requirement graph.

The recompute is what makes "after sync, the graph is up to date" true. The
event projection only moves rows that already exist, so a story coming back
into the graph (made ready, or reopened after a promotion) had no
requirements at all until something recomputed (2026-10-12, stories 1046 and
1092 at 0/0).
